blind_judge.simulator_quality: A feels comparatively natural and specific, though it repeats the pending layout check at turn 3. B’s repeated “registered that for verification” responses at turns 1, 2 and 4 feel mechanical and leave the customer with little useful information. Both transcripts end with follow-ups still pending.
blind_judge.summary: A wins because it answers the initial layout question with relevant facts and a useful clarifying question (turn 1), then adapts when the customer adds that her mother may stay over (turn 2). It also answers the maintenance/clubhouse question accurately and avoids inventing current charges (turns 3–4). A stronger turn 2 could give the known bedroom-area figures and explain that the plan depicts bedrooms accommodating queen-sized beds, while still cautioning that a desk-and-bed fit needs checking. B gives a useful maintenance/clubhouse distinction at turn 3, but otherwise mostly logs requests instead of addressing the customer’s layout needs or advancing the discussion.
